A question to ChatGPT:

User: No sorry I mean are the bednets causing this, from any source?

ChatGPT:

Yes. The worldwide scale-up of insecticide-treated bednets—from governments, the Global Fund, PMI, AMF, etc.—has been the largest single cause of the reduction in African malaria since 2000.
There are two levels of causal evidence:
Randomized trials found that treated nets reduced ordinary P. falciparum malaria episodes by about 45%, severe episodes by 44%, and all-cause mortality among young children by 17%. So the basic effect is experimental, not merely inferred from national trends. Cochrane review⁠�
A major 2015 attribution study reconstructed malaria prevalence and intervention coverage across Africa. It found that incidence fell about 40% from 2000–2015, with interventions averting an estimated 663 million cases. Bednets accounted for 68%—about 450 million—of those averted cases, versus 22% for artemisinin treatments and 10% for indoor spraying. Bhatt et al., Nature⁠�

The old way, so the new way makes sense

The first well-known scheme (Kirchenbauer's, 2023) did the obvious thing. Take a secret key, hash the previous token with it, and use that to randomly split the whole vocabulary into a "green list" and a "red list" — a fresh, unpredictable split at every single step. Then nudge: add a small constant to every green token's logit before sampling.
